THE PROFIT YOU DO NOT SEE

10 places where your bar
may be losing money.

These are examples of what the Mystery Guest Bar Audit looks for. How many happen in your bar?

  1. 01 / 10

    One pour too many. Margin too thin.

    Free pouring makes the cost of every drink unpredictable. The excess repeats, glass after glass.

    How to fix it

    Standardise measures and use a jigger.

  2. 02 / 10

    High sales. Little left over.

    Without drink specifications, you may sell cocktails without knowing what each one really costs.

    How to fix it

    Calculate the full cost of every recipe.

  3. 03 / 10

    Your neighbour’s prices do not pay your bills.

    Copying prices ignores your costs, your service and the margin you need.

    How to fix it

    Set prices based on cost and the value you deliver.

  4. 04 / 10

    Waste ends up on the bill too.

    Over-cut fruit, forgotten juices and excess prep add up to losses.

    How to fix it

    Prep to forecast demand and record waste.

  5. 05 / 10

    Without stock counts, losses hide.

    Without matching stock to sales, over-pours, comps and breakages go unnoticed.

    How to fix it

    Count stock and compare actual usage with expected usage.

  6. 06 / 10

    Idle bottles. Trapped cash.

    Buying products that barely sell ties up cash and takes up space.

    How to fix it

    Set purchasing and quantities by each product’s rotation.

  7. 07 / 10

    Does your menu know how to sell?

    Hiding high-margin, high-demand drinks wastes the potential of every order.

    How to fix it

    Highlight profitable choices with clear descriptions.

  8. 08 / 10

    The team serves. But can it recommend?

    Simply taking orders leaves choices unexplored that guests would value.

    How to fix it

    Train relevant suggestions, with clear prices and no pressure.

  9. 09 / 10

    Every minute of waiting can cost a sale.

    Poor prep and a disorganised station slow service at peak times.

    How to fix it

    Set up the station before opening and simplify movements.

  10. 10 / 10

    The wrong shift costs money.

    Too many staff in quiet hours and too few at peaks raise costs and lose sales.

    How to fix it

    Match shifts to demand and to the tasks of each period.

PRACTICAL QUESTIONS

Before you
move forward.

What is the difference between the Mystery Guest Bar Audit and the Full Audit?+

The Mystery Guest Bar Audit is a fixed-price diagnosis: 1 to 2 days in the bar as a guest and a report with at least 10 errors and improvements, for €990 + travel. The Full Audit is a tailored project with agreed objectives, an itemised quote and implementation on the ground: menus, QR menu, screens, training, a team on site and more.

What does the €990 Mystery Guest Bar Audit include?+

An assessment of 1 bar over 1 to 2 days on site as an anonymous guest, and a report within 7 days after the visit with at least 10 errors and improvements in order of priority. Travel is extra and agreed in advance. Prices exclude VAT. Implementation is part of the Full Audit.

How does the guarantee work?+

If the report does not identify at least 10 concrete errors and improvements, we refund the €990. Agreed travel costs are non-refundable.

Do I need the Mystery Guest before the Full Audit?+

It is not mandatory, but it is the recommended route: the diagnosis shows where the priorities are. If you go ahead within 30 days, the €990 is deducted from the quote.

What results should we expect?+

We define indicators around your operation: contribution margin, average spend, waste, consistency or service times. Outcomes depend on demand, resources and execution; we do not guarantee profits or revenue increases.

Do you work in Portugal and Spain?+

These are our priority markets. Location, travel and availability are confirmed for each project. You can get in touch in Portuguese, Spanish or English.

Is the Full Audit meeting really free?+

Yes. The on-site meeting carries no fee and no obligation. It is for getting to know the bar and agreeing objectives. We confirm availability and location; any travel cost is agreed beforehand.
